principles.statement: Model fluency and automaticity as multidimensional evidence; never reduce them to one raw speed, words-per-minute, pause-count or holistic percentage score.
Gate deliberate fluency practice on sufficient prior meaning, form and retrieval success; do not speed-train language that the learner still misunderstands or produces with unstable errors.
Record exact-item, same-content, task-family and communicative-function repetition provenance so local practice gains cannot be mistaken for unseen transfer.
Count temporal improvement positively only when meaning or task success and stage-appropriate accuracy, comprehension and intelligibility remain intact.

Use short bounded same-task repetition to reduce processing friction, then switch toward changed content or context; stop repetition when gains plateau, memorization dominates or quality trade-offs appear.
Require changed-task or changed-context performance before inferring portable fluency from practiced performance.
Require delayed changed-task or changed-context evidence before making strong automaticity, progression or mastery claims.
Keep automaticity evidence capability-, modality- and task-specific until transfer to another modality or operation is directly demonstrated.
For speaking, preserve speed, breakdown and repair evidence separately and interpret pauses, repetitions and reformulations in context rather than globally penalizing them.
Interpret speech timing relative to learner history, task conditions and personal or L1 speaking style; do not enforce one native-speaker-like temporal threshold as mastery.
Keep blocked, interleaved, massed and spaced practice schedules as adaptive and falsifiable product variables; do not hard-code a universal repetition count or interval as scientific truth.

Use shrinking time or other time pressure only after meaningful task success is established, and reduce or remove pressure when comprehension, accuracy, intelligibility or interaction quality deteriorates.
Treat useful chunks and formulaic sequences as reusable constructions: test slot substitution, new lexical content, changed scenario and interactional reuse rather than memorized recitation.
For listening, distinguish declarative sound-meaning recognition from prompt contextualized access; do not infer global listening improvement from faster target-item judgments alone.
For interaction, combine response timing with contingency, shared-goal progress, intelligibility and repair success; never optimize instant response latency in isolation.

Keep fluency-readiness thresholds, repetition dose, variation switch, spacing, time pressure, metric reliability, personal-style normalization and delayed-transfer criteria falsifiable until EXP-016 validates them for Vietnamese adults near A0/A1.
